body_markdown:
*Market data and industry research revealing how non-technical builders are reshaping software development through low-code and no-code platforms*


The citizen developer movement has evolved from an IT experiment into a core enterprise strategy. With the global citizen development platforms market[valued at $12.5 billion](https://datahorizzonresearch.com/citizen-development-platforms-market-46380) in 2024 and projected to reach $45.7 billion by 2033, organizations are rethinking who builds their applications.


For[non-technical founders](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) and business users, Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector for creating, editing, and publishing applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot manages the database, authentication, and hosting while the connected AI assistant handles development, within its connector permissions.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Citizen development is expanding:** The market is projected to grow at a[14.2% CAGR](https://datahorizzonresearch.com/citizen-development-platforms-market-46380) through 2033, creating opportunities for people using[Floot's app-building guide](https://floot.com/blog/how-to-build-full-stack-app-with-ai) .
- **Non-IT participation is rising:** Gartner forecast that[at least 80%](https://www.ciocan.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/CIO-White-Paper_Low-Code.FINAL_-1.pdf) of low-code users would come from outside IT by 2026;[Floot's connector docs](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) explain the AI-assisted approach.
- **Development can be faster:** Forrester described low-code development as[potentially 10x faster](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/why-you-need-to-know-about-low-code-even-if-youre-not-responsible-for-software-delivery/) for suitable applications;[Floot's MVP guide](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-mvp-development) covers a practical use case.
- **Workforce roles are changing:** Gartner forecast a[4-to-1 ratio](https://venturebeat.com/business/gartner-citizen-developers-will-soon-outnumber-professional-coders-4-to-1) of citizen to professional developers at large enterprises by 2023;[Floot's beginner guide](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) addresses non-technical builders.
- **AI-assisted building is gaining attention:** In KPMG's 2025 survey,[78% of organizations](https://hub.kpmg.de/study-low-code-ai-accelerating-digital-transformation) were developing or planning AI-powered low-code applications; Floot's[MCP explainer](https://floot.com/blog/what-is-mcp-a-simple-guide-to-model-context-protocol-for-ai-apps) provides context.


## **The Rise of the Citizen Developer: Market Size and Growth**


The citizen development platforms market represents one of the fastest-growing segments in enterprise technology. These numbers reveal why businesses are investing heavily in tools that empower non-technical users to build applications.


### **1. Market valued at $12.5 billion in 2024**


The global citizen development platforms market was valued at[$12.5 billion](https://datahorizzonresearch.com/citizen-development-platforms-market-46380) in 2024, establishing a substantial foundation for continued growth. DataHorizzon Research's analysis indicates this market segment encompasses visual development environments, low-code platforms, and no-code tools designed specifically for business users. The valuation reflects enterprise investment in democratizing application development beyond traditional IT departments.


### **2. Projected growth to $45.7 billion by 2033**


Industry projections indicate the market could[reach $45.7 billion](https://datahorizzonresearch.com/citizen-development-platforms-market-46380) by 2033, representing nearly four times current valuations. This expansion reflects enterprise recognition that citizen development addresses persistent developer shortages while accelerating digital transformation initiatives. Market analysts attribute growth to increasing platform sophistication, AI integration, and expanding use cases beyond simple workflow automation.


### **3. 14.2% CAGR through 2033**


The citizen development platforms market is projected to grow at a[14.2% compound annual growth rate](https://datahorizzonresearch.com/citizen-development-platforms-market-46380) from 2025 to 2033. This projected double-digit growth would exceed many enterprise software categories, driven by platform maturity, governance frameworks, and integration capabilities that make citizen-built applications viable for production use. Regional expansion in Asia-Pacific and increased adoption among mid-market companies contribute to sustained momentum.


### **4. Low-code market valued at $37.8 billion in 2025**


The broader low-code application development platform market was[valued at $37.8 billion](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) in 2025. Grand View Research's measurement encompasses both citizen developer tools and professional low-code platforms used by IT departments. The larger market size reflects enterprise adoption of low-code methodologies across the entire application lifecycle, from rapid prototyping to mission-critical system development.


### **5. Low-code market projected to reach $115.2 billion by 2033**


The low-code application development platform market is projected to[reach $115.2 billion](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) by 2033, according to Grand View Research. This forecast assumes continued enterprise digital transformation, hybrid work environments requiring custom applications, and platform evolution incorporating AI-assisted development. The projection represents the broader low-code category including both citizen and professional developer tools.


### **6. 15.0% CAGR projected for low-code platforms**


The low-code application development platform market is projected to grow at a[15.0% CAGR](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) from 2026 to 2033. This growth rate reflects increasing enterprise comfort with low-code for production applications, improved security and governance capabilities, and expanding integration ecosystems that connect low-code platforms to existing enterprise systems. The forecast also reflects rising interest in AI-assisted software development.


### **7. North America commands 38% of the market**


North America[accounts for roughly 38%](https://datahorizzonresearch.com/citizen-development-platforms-market-46380) of the global citizen development platforms market, reflecting strong enterprise adoption. The region's dominance stems from early low-code platform adoption, significant venture investment in no-code startups, and regulatory environments that encourage IT modernization. However, Asia-Pacific represents the fastest-growing regional market as digital transformation accelerates across emerging economies.


### **8. Platforms represented over 68% of market revenue in 2025**


The platform segment accounted for[over 68% of low-code](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) application development platform market revenue in 2025. This component includes core platform subscriptions, development environments, and runtime infrastructure. The remaining revenue comes from professional services, training, and third-party extensions. Platform revenue dominance indicates that enterprises prioritize subscription access over one-time services engagements.


## **Organizational Adoption: How Companies Are Embracing Citizen Development**


Enterprises across industries are actively integrating citizen developers into their software strategies. These statistics demonstrate the breadth of adoption.


### **9. 41% of organizations had citizen development initiatives**


A Gartner survey cited in a 2022 industry report found that[41% of organizations](https://f.hubspotusercontent40.net/hubfs/1624046/R-WP_RoleandInfluence_02.22.22.pdf) had active citizen development initiatives, with another 20% evaluating or planning them. The figure describes Gartner's 2020 measurement, not a current 2027 adoption rate. It illustrates how businesses began formalizing application-building roles outside traditional IT teams before more recent AI-assisted development tools became widely available.


### **10. 37% have made low-code central to development strategy**


In KPMG's 2025 survey,[37% of organizations](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) had made low-code central to their overall software development strategies. KPMG's 2025 research indicates these organizations integrate low-code tools into their technology roadmaps, establish centers of excellence, and allocate budget specifically for citizen development initiatives. The figure describes stated strategic adoption, not a guaranteed improvement in business performance.


### **11. Gartner projected 70% low-code adoption for new enterprise apps by 2025**


Gartner projected in 2021 that[70% of new applications](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/85-of-organizations-will-be-cloud-first-by-2025-says-gartner/) developed by enterprises would use low-code or no-code technologies by 2025, up from less than 25% in 2020. This forecast anticipated rapid low-code adoption driven by developer shortages and accelerating digital transformation demands. While actual adoption rates vary by industry and organization size, low-code has become mainstream for many application categories.


### **12. 64% of digital leaders have made low-code central to development**


KPMG's 2025 research found that[64% of digital leaders](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) had integrated low-code into their software development strategies. The study surveyed 2,170 executives across industries and found that organizations with advanced digital maturity were significantly more likely to embrace low-code than those in early transformation stages. Strategic integration includes governance frameworks, security protocols, and IT collaboration models.


## **The Workforce Transformation: Citizen vs. Professional Developers**


The balance between traditional IT developers and business users who build applications is shifting dramatically. For those exploring[full-stack apps with AI](https://floot.com/blog/how-to-build-full-stack-app-with-ai) , these workforce statistics highlight why the opportunity is significant.


### **13. Gartner projected a 4-to-1 citizen-to-professional developer ratio**


Gartner projected that active citizen developers would outnumber professional developers by[4 to 1](https://venturebeat.com/business/gartner-citizen-developers-will-soon-outnumber-professional-coders-4-to-1) at large enterprises by 2023. This forecast assumed that low-code tools would enable business users across departments to build departmental applications, automated workflows, and data dashboards. The projection highlighted the potential scale of citizen development when organizations implement appropriate governance and training programs.


### **14. Gartner projected 80% of low-code users would be non-IT by 2026**


Gartner projected that, by 2026,[at least 80%](https://www.ciocan.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/CIO-White-Paper_Low-Code.FINAL_-1.pdf) of users of low-code development tools would come from outside formal IT departments, up from 60% in 2021. This forecast reflected platform vendors' focus on user experience, visual development interfaces, and AI-assisted development that reduce technical prerequisites. The prediction anticipated continued democratization of application development across business functions.


### **15. Nearly 60% of custom apps were built outside IT in 2017**


A 2017 research report found that[nearly 60% of apps](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/report-60-of-apps-are-built-outside-of-it-and-thats-a-good-thing/) were built outside the IT department, with a substantial share created by employees with limited technical training. This historical measurement captured early citizen development activity before modern low-code platforms matured. The statistic demonstrated that business users were already building applications through spreadsheet macros, database tools, and early workflow automation platforms.


### **16. Gartner projected 80% of tech products would be built outside IT by 2024**


Gartner projected that[80% of technology products](https://venturebeat.com/technology/80-of-tech-could-be-built-outside-it-by-2024-thanks-to-low-code-tools) and services would be built by professionals outside of IT by 2024. This broader forecast extended beyond internal applications to encompass customer-facing digital products, suggesting that product managers, designers, and business analysts would increasingly use low-code tools for prototyping and production development. The projection anticipated platform evolution toward full-stack capabilities.


### **17. Forrester reported 87% of enterprise developers used low-code in 2024**


[87% of enterprise developers](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/the-low-code-market-could-approach-50-billion-by-2028/) used low-code for at least some of their development work, according to research discussed by Forrester in January 2024. The report found that professional developers increasingly incorporate low-code platforms into their workflow for rapid prototyping, internal tools, and components of larger applications. This statistic challenges the perception that low-code serves only citizen developers, demonstrating its value for accelerating professional development.


## **Performance and Efficiency: The Business Case for Citizen Development**


The productivity benefits of citizen development tools vary by application and implementation. These metrics explain why platforms enabling[MVP development](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-mvp-development) through low-code approaches continue gaining traction.


### **18. Development can be 10x faster**


Low-code application development can be[potentially 10x faster](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/why-you-need-to-know-about-low-code-even-if-youre-not-responsible-for-software-delivery/) than traditional application development methods. Forrester's 2018 analysis identified time savings from pre-built components, visual development interfaces, and automatic code generation. The potential speed improvement applies primarily to applications matching low-code platform strengths, such as data-driven business applications, rather than complex custom algorithms or high-performance systems.


### **19. Research reviewed 226 studies on low-code development**


A 2026 systematic literature review analyzed[226 studies](https://research.aalto.fi/en/publications/what-does-current-research-say-about-the-viability-of-low-code-de/) and found evidence that low-code accelerates development, while outcomes for cost, security, and complexity require additional investigation. The academic review examined empirical research on low-code platforms and identified gaps in current understanding, particularly around long-term maintenance costs and security implications. The study called for more rigorous measurement of low-code outcomes.


### **20. 52% report better process efficiency**


[52% of surveyed executives](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) reported better process efficiency after adopting low-code solutions. KPMG's 2025 study found that process improvements extended beyond IT to business operations, as departmental teams built applications addressing specific workflow bottlenecks. The result reflects respondents' perceptions of efficiency improvements, not a universal performance guarantee.


### **21. 48% see improved product quality**


[48% of surveyed executives](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) reported better service or product quality from low-code adoption. Potential reasons include faster iteration, more opportunities for testing, and closer collaboration between business stakeholders and builders. The reported result does not establish that these benefits occur automatically or for every application.


### **22. 46% experience higher employee productivity**


[46% of surveyed executives](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) reported higher employee productivity after implementing low-code tools. Productivity gains occurred across both IT departments and business units, as developers focused on complex challenges while business users built departmental applications. The result should be read as a survey response rather than as a measured productivity increase across every organization.


### **23. 39% achieved cost reduction**


[39% of surveyed executives](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) identified cost reduction as a direct benefit of low-code adoption. Potential savings can arise from shorter development cycles and less manual implementation work. Actual savings depend on subscription expenses, training requirements, and the complexity of the applications built.


### **24. 33% higher innovation scores associated with citizen development**


McKinsey found that companies empowering citizen developers scored[33% higher](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/technology-media-and-telecommunications/our-insights/developer-velocity-how-software-excellence-fuels-business-performance) than bottom-quartile companies in its 2020 research. Innovation was one of several nonfinancial performance indicators considered in McKinsey's developer-velocity research. The reported correlation does not prove citizen development alone caused the difference in innovation scores.


## **The IT Backlog Crisis: Why Citizen Development Matters**


IT departments face persistent resource constraints that citizen development helps address. Understanding the[MCP protocol](https://floot.com/blog/what-is-mcp-a-simple-guide-to-model-context-protocol-for-ai-apps) and conversational development tools like Floot provides one path to reducing these backlogs.


### **25. Backlogs range from 3 to 12 months**


A 2021 Economist Intelligence Unit study reported that the average backlog for planned IT projects ranged from[3 to 12 months](https://cioaxis.com/just-in/83-of-it-leaders-say-adapting-to-change-requires-better-apps-and-infrastructure/amp) . The research surveyed 1,002 IT and business decision-makers and examined the challenges of delivering technology initiatives in changing business environments. Extended backlogs create business opportunity costs when competitive demands require faster application delivery.


### **26. About 106,100 annual U.S. software developer, QA analyst, and tester openings projected**


The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects approximately[106,100 annual openings](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/computer-and-information-technology/software-developers.htm) for software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers from 2025 to 2035. This projection accounts for both employment growth and replacement needs as workers leave the occupation. The steady demand for developers reinforces the value of citizen development as a complementary strategy rather than a complete replacement for professional development.


### **27. Software developer employment projected to grow by 174.7 thousand U.S. jobs**


U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projections indicate that software developer employment could increase by[approximately 174.7 thousand](https://www.bls.gov/emp/skills/computers-and-information-technology.htm) jobs between 2025 and 2035. This employment growth reflects continued digital transformation across industries, though it may not fully satisfy enterprise demand for application development. This forecast indicates continued demand for professional development skills alongside opportunities for citizen developers.


### **28. Software developer employment projected to grow 10.2% through 2035**


U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projections indicate that employment of software developers could[grow by 10.2%](https://www.bls.gov/emp/skills/computers-and-information-technology.htm) between 2025 and 2035. That is more than three times the roughly 3% growth projected for U.S. occupations overall. The projection reinforces that citizen development is a complementary option, not a replacement for trained software professionals.


## **AI Integration and Strategic Priorities**


The convergence of AI and citizen development is reshaping how applications are created. Platforms like Floot that integrate with existing AI assistants through[AI assistant connectors](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) can support this shift. Builders can also read Floot's[platform comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-cursor-which-ai-development-tool-is-right-for-you-in-2026) for how AI coding tools work alongside managed infrastructure.


### **29. 78% developing AI-powered low-code apps**


[78% of surveyed organizations](https://hub.kpmg.de/study-low-code-ai-accelerating-digital-transformation) were developing or planned to develop AI-powered low-code applications within 12 months, according to KPMG in 2025. KPMG's 2025 research found that AI integration represents a top strategic priority, with organizations exploring generative AI for application generation, intelligent workflows, and enhanced user experiences. Early implementations focus on AI-assisted development tools and AI features within citizen-built applications.


### **30. Strategic importance rose from 31% to 44%**


[44% of companies](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) considered low-code development strategically important, up from 31% in 2022. The increase indicates stronger reported strategic interest but does not, on its own, establish return on investment. Organizations elevating low-code to strategic importance typically establish governance frameworks and centers of excellence.


### **31. 85% prioritize security in platform selection**


[85% of surveyed executives](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) rated security as important or very important when selecting a low-code platform. Security considerations include data protection, access controls, compliance with regulatory requirements, and vulnerability management. Organizations emphasized that platform security features must complement governance policies defining what citizen developers can build and which data sources they can access.


### **32. 84% prioritize ease of integration**


[84% of surveyed executives](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) rated ease of integration as important or very important in their platform decisions. Integration capabilities determine whether citizen-built applications can connect to enterprise systems, external APIs, and data sources. Organizations prioritize platforms offering pre-built connectors, standard APIs, and authentication mechanisms that work within existing IT architecture rather than requiring custom development.


### **33. 52% plan citizen developers for most applications**


[52% of surveyed executives](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) said their companies planned to use citizen developers for most low-code applications. This strategic approach positions IT as enablers providing platforms, governance, and architecture guidance while empowering business units to build departmental applications. Organizations adopting this model typically establish training programs and support structures for citizen developers.


### **34. 42% focus citizen developers on simpler apps**


[42% of surveyed organizations](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) planned to use citizen developers mainly for less complex applications. This approach reserves sophisticated applications for professional developers while enabling business users to build workflow automation, data dashboards, and departmental tools. Organizations using this model typically define complexity criteria distinguishing citizen developer projects from those requiring IT involvement.


### **35. 39% have or plan governance rules**


[39% of surveyed organizations](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) had introduced low-code governance rules or were in final planning stages. Governance frameworks typically address application approval workflows, security requirements, data access policies, and testing standards. The statistic measures governance adoption or planned adoption, not the effectiveness of those governance rules.


## **Team Adoption and Department Usage Patterns**


Citizen development has spread across organizational functions, with various teams building applications to solve their specific challenges. The[Floot showcase](https://floot.com/en/showcase) demonstrates the diversity of applications now built by non-technical users.


### **36. Gartner projected 75% of large enterprises would use 4+ low-code tools by 2025**


Gartner projected that[75% of large enterprises](https://kpmg.com/sk/en/insights/2023/05/low-code-high-value-for-digital-transformation.html) would use at least four low-code development tools for IT application development and citizen development initiatives by 2025. This multi-platform prediction anticipated that organizations would use specialized tools for different use cases rather than standardizing on a single platform, reflecting the diversity of application requirements across enterprise departments.


### **37. 42% of business technologists used purpose-built tools in Gartner research**


Gartner reported that only[42% of business technologists](https://venturebeat.com/business/gartner-citizen-developers-will-soon-outnumber-professional-coders-4-to-1) used technology tools designed specifically for their roles in research discussed in 2021. This population included people building or customizing tools outside formal IT departments and was broader than citizen developers alone. The finding illustrates a gap between employees who create technology solutions and the availability of tools tailored to their needs. It does not measure the adoption of any particular platform in 2027.


### **38. IDC projects over 1 billion net-new applications by 2028**


IDC research cited by VMware[projects over 1 billion](https://blogs.vmware.com/cloud-foundation/2025/10/27/idc-spotlight-overcoming-kubernetes-complexity-with-modern-private-cloud/) net-new applications by 2028. This is a forecast for cloud-native applications overall, not a count limited to citizen-developed or low-code applications. The projection assumes continued digital transformation, edge computing expansion, and increasing application modularity enabling smaller, more specialized software components.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What exactly is a citizen developer?**


A citizen developer is a non-IT professional who creates applications using low-code or no-code platforms. These individuals typically work in business roles like marketing, operations, or product management and build tools to solve departmental challenges without formal programming training. Modern platforms enable citizen developers to create increasingly sophisticated applications including web apps, mobile experiences, and workflow automation through visual interfaces or conversational AI.


### **How do low-code and no-code platforms differ?**


Low-code platforms may require some technical knowledge and limited custom code, while no-code platforms allow users to build through visual interfaces or natural-language instructions. Floot combines full-stack app infrastructure with an MCP connector: a supported AI assistant performs the development work, subject to its permissions, and Floot manages hosting, database, and authentication. See the[Floot connector guide](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) for supported workflows.


### **Can citizen developers really build production-ready applications?**


Yes, depending on the application and the testing performed. Floot provides managed databases, authentication, hosting, and deployment tools, but production readiness still requires appropriate security, performance, and usability testing. Teams should also establish suitable governance and IT review processes for sensitive data and enterprise integrations. The[Floot platform comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-cursor-which-ai-development-tool-is-right-for-you-in-2026) explains how a connected development assistant can work alongside Floot infrastructure.


### **What types of applications do citizen developers typically build?**


Citizen developers build a wide range of applications including internal tools, customer-facing websites, mobile apps, workflow automation, and data dashboards. Teams across engineering, analytics, marketing, product, operations, and sales use low-code tools to address their specific needs. Common use cases include approval workflows, data collection forms, reporting dashboards, customer portals, and departmental productivity tools that would otherwise wait in IT backlogs.


### **How does AI change citizen development?**


AI enables conversational development, where users describe the application they want instead of writing all the code themselves. Floot connects supported Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT workflows to managed app infrastructure, with capabilities depending on connector permissions. The AI assistant performs development; Floot supplies hosting, database, and authentication. Builders can check[current Floot pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) for plan limits and hosting charges, which are separate from their existing AI subscriptions.
